module.label: Users
module.title: User Management
module.summary: Manage corporate users within the authenticated operator's approved partner and source scope.

nodes.title: User list ready
nodes.subtitle: Choose a table action or a user

flows.title: Open and load corporate users
flows.summary: Load only the corporate users belonging to the operator's authorized partner scope and distinguish loading, empty, error, and unauthorized states.
preconditions: The operator is authenticated.
The login state contains the corporate user ID and portal source.
The operator is authorized to view users.
flows.outcome: The authorized user list is visible, or a distinct empty, error, or unauthorized state is shown.

steps.title: Open Users
steps.detail: The operator selects Users in the portal navigation.

steps.title: Build scoped request
steps.detail: The page uses the logged-in user ID as partner_id and includes the portal source.

steps.title: Request users
steps.detail: POST /jane/getCorpUsers while the page displays a loading state.

steps.title: Was the request successful?
steps.detail: Separate successful data, successful empty, unauthorized, and technical failure outcomes.

steps.title: Render the correct state
steps.detail: Store authorized users in Redux or show the appropriate empty/error state with Retry when applicable.

branches.label: Users returned
branches.detail: Store and display only users returned for the authorized partner scope.

branches.label: Empty result
branches.detail: Show No users found without describing the outcome as an error.

branches.label: Technical failure
branches.detail: Show a recoverable error with Retry; do not present it as an empty list.

branches.label: Unauthorized
branches.detail: Deny route access and do not expose user data.

apis.name: getCorpUsers
apis.purpose: Load users for the authenticated corporate partner.

rules.text: An operator may view and manage only users in the authorized partner or tenant scope.
The backend must enforce permissions and tenant boundaries independently of the browser.

gaps.text: Fine-grained permission enforcement is not verified for the Users route and actions.
Current request failures normally appear as an empty user list.

acceptance.text: A successful request displays only users returned for the operator's partner scope.
Pending requests show loading and disable destructive actions.
A successful empty response shows No users found.
A technical failure shows an error with Retry.
Unauthorized operators cannot access the route or retrieve the list.

flows.title: Search, sort, paginate and export
flows.trigger: Use a table control after users have loaded.
flows.summary: Explore the already-loaded user list and export the current authorized result without exposing action or internal fields.
preconditions: The user list has completed loading.
The operator has View Users permission.
Export additionally requires Export Users permission.
flows.outcome: The table or CSV reflects the current search and sort result.

steps.title: Choose a table operation
steps.detail: Enter a search, select a sortable column, change page or page size, or request export.

steps.title: Transform loaded rows
steps.detail: Apply case-insensitive search, sorting, and pagination to the authorized in-memory list.

steps.title: Export requested?
steps.detail: Check the independent export permission before preparing a file.

steps.title: Show or export result
steps.detail: Update row range and totals, or download the filtered result without Actions and internal fields.

branches.label: Search cleared
branches.detail: Restore the full loaded list and reset to page 1.

branches.label: Page size changed
branches.detail: Reset to page 1 before rendering the new range.

branches.label: Export denied
branches.detail: Do not generate or download user data.

rules.text: Table operations must remain limited to users in the authorized scope.

gaps.text: CSV export is disabled by the exportcsv versus exportCsv prop-name mismatch.
The initial page size is 10, but 10 is absent from the page-size options.

acceptance.text: A partial mixed-case email search returns the correct rows.
Selecting a sortable column twice toggles ascending and descending order.
The visible range and total match the filtered result.
CSV contains the filtered users and excludes the Actions column.
An operator without Export permission cannot export.

flows.title: Create corporate user
flows.summary: Validate and create exactly one corporate user in the intended partner and source scope.
preconditions: The operator is authenticated and authorized to create users.
The authoritative partner and source are known.
flows.outcome: One new user is created and appears once in the list.

steps.title: Open Add User
steps.detail: Display a blank form with approved defaults and the corporate email read-only.

steps.title: Enter profile
steps.detail: Provide first name, last name, work email, international phone number, and status.

steps.title: Normalize and validate
steps.detail: Trim inputs and validate required names, email format, phone format, and approved source scope.

steps.title: Is the submission valid?
steps.detail: Block invalid or duplicate values with field-level guidance.

steps.title: Create user
steps.detail: Disable repeat submission and POST addCorpUser with requestType Add.

steps.title: Refresh list
steps.detail: Close the modal, show confirmation, and append exactly one authoritative response row.

branches.label: Validation failure
branches.detail: Keep the form open and show field-level errors.

branches.label: Duplicate user
branches.detail: Preserve entered values and display an understandable conflict message.

branches.label: API failure
branches.detail: Keep data, re-enable Create, and offer retry.

rules.text: Email is the user ID and becomes immutable after creation.
First name, last name, valid email, and valid international phone are mandatory.
Repeated submission must not create duplicate users.

gaps.text: Create is not currently protected against repeated clicks.
Create always uses urwifi while other flows derive source differently.
Required fields currently use truthy checks instead of normalized validation.
Card lookup runs before the new user has a persisted identity.

acceptance.text: Blank or whitespace-only required values block submission.
Invalid email blocks submission.
Invalid or incomplete phone blocks submission.
A pending create cannot be submitted twice.
Success closes the modal and shows exactly one new row.
Duplicate-user failure preserves entered data and explains the conflict.
The user is linked only to the approved partner and source.

flows.title: Edit corporate user
flows.trigger: Select Edit for an existing user.
flows.summary: Update permitted profile fields while preserving immutable identity and authoritative partner/source ownership.
preconditions: A user row is selected.
The operator may edit that user.
The current authoritative record is available.
flows.outcome: Saved values appear immediately in the selected row.

steps.title: Select Edit
steps.detail: Open a mode-specific edit form populated from the selected row.

steps.title: Lock identifiers
steps.detail: Email, phone, partner, and source remain read-only unless a separate migration flow exists.

steps.title: Change permitted values
steps.detail: Edit first name, last name, and approved status fields.

steps.title: Any valid changes?
steps.detail: Enable Save only when normalized values differ and remain valid.

steps.title: Save update
steps.detail: POST addCorpUser with requestType Edit and authoritative user identifiers.

steps.title: Update row
steps.detail: Apply an immutable state update and close or confirm the modal according to policy.

branches.label: Close with unsaved changes
branches.detail: Ask the operator to discard or continue editing.

branches.label: Concurrent update
branches.detail: Use version handling or an explicitly approved last-write-wins rule.

branches.label: Save failure
branches.detail: Preserve changes and display the backend message.

rules.text: Email is immutable after creation.
Phone changes require a separate verified process.
Profile changes must be audited.

gaps.text: The reducer mutates the existing user array and may not trigger a reliable re-render.
Edit source is inferred from the operator instead of an approved authoritative rule.
The Edit modal subtitle currently describes creating a new user.

acceptance.text: Email and phone cannot be edited through this flow.
Save includes the selected user ID and approved partner/source scope.
The list updates immediately after success.
Failure preserves edits and displays the backend message.
Closing a dirty form requires confirmation.

flows.title: Suspend or reactivate user
flows.trigger: Select Suspend for an active user or Reactivate for a suspended user.
flows.summary: Change lifecycle status with confirmation, visible outcome, preserved history, and an audit record.
preconditions: The selected user exists.
The operator may change status.
The requested transition is permitted by policy.
flows.outcome: The status changes only after backend success and the transition is audited.

steps.title: Choose status action
steps.detail: Select Suspend or Reactivate for the user.

steps.title: Explain impact
steps.detail: Show what the transition means for sign-in, orders, devices, plans, and billing.

steps.title: Confirm transition?
steps.detail: Cancel leaves the status unchanged and sends no request.

steps.title: Submit status
steps.detail: Send an Edit request with active 0 or 1 while preventing duplicates.

steps.title: Update and audit
steps.detail: Change the visible row only after success and record actor, user, old/new state, time, and reason when required.

branches.label: Canceled
branches.detail: No API call and no visual status change.

branches.label: Failure
branches.detail: Keep the previous status and show a recoverable error.

branches.label: Policy blocks transition
branches.detail: Explain why the selected transition is unavailable.

rules.text: A user has one approved lifecycle status.
Suspension is reversible and preserves history.
Status changes must be audited.

gaps.text: Current Suspend sends immediately without confirmation or visible API result.
The Japanese tooltip currently describes Suspend as deletion.

acceptance.text: Canceling confirmation sends no request.
Status changes only after backend success.
Failure leaves the displayed status unchanged and shows an error.
Audit data identifies actor, user, old/new status, timestamp, and reason when required.
An authorized operator can reactivate when policy permits.

flows.title: Delete user
flows.trigger: Select Delete User from Edit mode.
flows.summary: Permanently delete only when policy, retention rules, dependencies, authorization, and explicit confirmation all permit it; otherwise use Suspend or Archive.
preconditions: Management has approved hard deletion.
The user has no protected dependencies.
The operator has Delete Users permission.
flows.outcome: The row is removed only after confirmed backend success, with an immutable audit event.

steps.title: Request deletion
steps.detail: Select Delete User for the chosen record.

steps.title: Check policy and dependencies
steps.detail: Verify retention, financial records, order history, privacy obligations, and authorization.

steps.title: Is deletion permitted?
steps.detail: If not, explain the block and direct the operator to Suspend or Archive.

steps.title: Confirm irreversible action
steps.detail: Require an explicit confirmation that identifies the selected user.

steps.title: Delete and audit
steps.detail: POST deleteUser and create an immutable audit event.

steps.title: Remove after success
steps.detail: Remove the row exactly once only after the backend confirms deletion.

branches.label: Not approved
branches.detail: Hide or disable Delete and use the approved reversible action.

branches.label: Dependency blocks deletion
branches.detail: Keep the user and explain the applicable retention rule.

branches.label: Request rejected or failed
branches.detail: Keep the row and modal unchanged and display the reason.

apis.name: deleteUser
apis.purpose: Delete the selected user when policy allows it.

errorResponse.message: User cannot be deleted because protected records exist

rules.text: Deleted or archived state follows the approved lifecycle policy.
Hard deletion remains disabled unless retention and dependency checks permit it.
Deletion must be audited.

gaps.text: DELETEUSER is missing from action constants and the reducer, so the row may remain visible.
The current modal closes after an unsuccessful response.

acceptance.text: No deletion request is sent without explicit confirmation.
Successful approved deletion removes the row exactly once.
Rejected deletion keeps the row and displays the reason.
Protected history follows the approved retention rule.
Unauthorized operators cannot see or invoke Delete.

flows.title: Assign corporate card
flows.trigger: Choose Assign corporate card while editing a user without an existing corporate card.
flows.summary: Associate one eligible corporate card with a user using masked information and idempotent behavior.
preconditions: The user has no current crpc card.
The corporate account has an eligible card.
The operator has Card Assignment permission.
flows.outcome: The user has one audited corporate-card association and only masked card information is displayed.

steps.title: Load association state
steps.detail: Determine whether the selected user already has a crpc card.

steps.title: Eligible corporate card available?
steps.detail: Block assignment when the corporate account has no eligible card.

steps.title: Choose assignment
steps.detail: Select the checkbox after reviewing masked card information.

steps.title: Submit with user edit
steps.detail: Set isAssignCard only when no association exists and prevent duplicate requests.

steps.title: Show masked association
steps.detail: Refresh card data and record actor, user, masked reference, and time.

branches.label: No corporate card
branches.detail: Disable assignment and explain that the corporate account needs an eligible card.

branches.label: Association already exists
branches.detail: Do not offer duplicate assignment.

branches.label: Partial failure
branches.detail: Do not report the full edit as successful until atomic versus partial behavior is defined.

apis.name: addCorpUser
apis.purpose: Update the user and request corporate-card assignment.

rules.text: A user may have at most one corporate card unless multiple-card support is approved.
Only masked card information may be shown.
Repeated submission must not create duplicate associations.

gaps.text: Card data is requested in Add mode before a persisted user identity exists.

acceptance.text: Assignment is unavailable when no eligible corporate card exists.
An existing association cannot be duplicated.
Success displays masked card information only.
The audit event identifies actor, user, masked reference, and timestamp.

flows.title: Remove corporate card
flows.trigger: Select the card removal action for a user with a crpc card.
flows.summary: Unassign the current corporate card after confirmation while preserving the association on failure.
preconditions: A crpc card association exists.
The operator has Card Assignment permission.
The billing impact is defined.
flows.outcome: The card association is removed after success and the operation is audited.

steps.title: Show current card
steps.detail: Display masked last digits and never expose full card data.

steps.title: Choose Unassign
steps.detail: Use business wording that matches whether the backend unassigns or deletes a payment method.

steps.title: Explain billing impact
steps.detail: Describe what happens to future billing before confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm removal?
steps.detail: Cancel leaves the association unchanged.

steps.title: Submit removal
steps.detail: Send cardId, user email, and app user ID to the dispatcher.

steps.title: Refresh association
steps.detail: After success, replace masked-card details with the assignment option.

branches.label: Canceled
branches.detail: Do not call the dispatcher or change the card display.

branches.label: Failure
branches.detail: Keep the current masked association and offer a recoverable error.

branches.label: Semantics unresolved
branches.detail: Confirm whether deleteCard removes a payment method or only its user association.

apis.name: deleteCard
apis.purpose: Remove or unassign the selected corporate-card association.

rules.text: Corporate-card association follows the approved one-card policy.
Only masked card information may be shown.
Card removal must be audited.

gaps.text: Card-removal exceptions currently provide no visible recovery state.

acceptance.text: Canceling confirmation leaves the association unchanged.
Success replaces masked-card details with the assignment option.
Failure preserves the card display and shows an error.

flows.title: Open user in Support
flows.trigger: Select Support for a user row that contains an email.
flows.summary: Carry the selected user's email into Support and initiate the correct lookup without bypassing Support authorization or tenant scope.
preconditions: The row contains an email.
The operator is authorized to access Support.
Support independently enforces tenant scope.
flows.outcome: Support opens and searches for the intended user within the operator's authorized scope.

steps.title: Select Support
steps.detail: Choose the Support action on the intended user row.

steps.title: Carry navigation context
steps.detail: Navigate to /admin/support with prefillUserQuery set to the selected email.

steps.title: Prefill and search
steps.detail: Support copies the email into its query and runs the Email/Mobile lookup.

steps.title: Clear transient state
steps.detail: Remove the navigation state after consuming it.

steps.title: Show authorized result
steps.detail: Display the selected user only if independent Support authorization and scope checks pass.

branches.label: Email missing
branches.detail: Disable the Support action and explain why it is unavailable.

branches.label: Support unauthorized
branches.detail: Deny access; navigation context must never grant permission.

branches.label: User not found
branches.detail: Show the standard Support no-result state.

rules.text: Support lookup remains restricted to authorized tenant scope.
Support authorization must be enforced independently of navigation state.

acceptance.text: Selecting Support opens the page and initiates lookup for the correct email.
Missing email disables the action with an explanatory tooltip.
Support independently checks authorization and partner scope.
